extracted.intended_audience: general newspaper readers interested in wartime national and international news
extracted.subtask_description: A multi-topic wartime newspaper report (labor controls, tax reform proposals, military actions and foreign measures) summarizing government orders, policy proposals, and battlefield dispatches for a general readership.

rubrics_metrics.name: WMC control of hiring in critical labor-shortage areas
rubrics_metrics.description: The War Manpower Commission (WMC) would take control of the hiring of labor in shortage areas, furnishing workers to employers on a priority system based on the employer's importance to the war effort and placing limits on worker shifts from vital occupations to less essential ones.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Text: “Nutt announced tonight that the War Manpower commission would take control of the hiring of labor in shortage areas... Under the system, Mr. McNutt said, the manpower commission or agencies approved by it will furnish workers to employers on a priority system based on the importance of the employer in the war effort. New barriers will be raised to prevent workers shifting from vital occupations to less essential ones, and limits will be placed...” Also: controls to go into effect “as soon as practicable” in “critical labor shortage areas”; a list of 32 localities was issued but subject to change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority-based allocation of workers
rubrics_metrics.description: Hiring agencies are directed to accord priority to employers engaged in essential activities, in the order of the urgency of their activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quoted directive: “Accord priority to employers engaged in essential activities, in the order of the urgency of their activities x x x.” This is presented as a principal organizing rule for the WMC allocation system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Placement on basis of qualifications and non-discrimination
rubrics_metrics.description: Workers are to be placed in jobs on the basis of their qualifications and without discrimination as to race, creed, sex, national origin.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stated hiring directive: “Place workers in jobs on ‘the basis of their qualifications’ and without discrimination as to race; creed, sex, national origin...” Emphasis in story that placements should be merit- and qualification-based while forbidding discrimination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use and coordination of existing hiring channels
rubrics_metrics.description: Principal hiring operations to be handled through the U.S. Employment Service but with 'maximum utilization' of all existing hiring channels (private employers, labor organizations, professional organizations, schools, technical institutions, government agencies).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Text: “The principal hiring operations will be handled through the U. S. Employment Service, but the order directed ‘maximum utilization’ of ‘all existing hiring channels’ which would operate under WMC policy regulations. Specifically... ‘channels’ were private employers, labor organizations, professional organizations, schools, technical institutions, and government agencies.” Also instructs hiring agencies to utilize skills most effectively in war effort.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local operation and consultation requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Local hiring control programs must conform to broad WMC headquarters policy and be operated/regulated by area directors who are to consult area management-labor committees and local leaders of management and labor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Story: “While provision was made for adjustment to local conditions... local hiring control programs in general must conform to broad WMC headquarters [policy]... otherwise they will be operated and regulated by area directors, who are to ‘consult’ area management-labor committees. Officials emphasized that the programs be operated in a democratic way, with full regard to local conditions and with the advice of local leaders of management and labor.”

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceptions to WMC supervision
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain hirings are exempt from WMC supervision: hiring by small establishments (generally defined as non-manufacturing establishments employing less than 25 persons and manufacturing firms employing less than eight persons), hiring of domestic servants or 'casual' (temporary) employees, and hiring by state/county/local governments unless they voluntarily request to be under WMC regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quoted exceptions: “except: 1. That done by small establishments, which ‘in general’ are defined as non-manufacturing establishments employing less than 25 Persons and manufacturing firms employing less than eight persons. 2. The hiring of domestic servants or ‘casual’ (temporary) employees, 3. Hiring by state, county or local governments, unless they ‘voluntarily request’ that they be put under WMC regulations.”

rubrics_metrics.name: Release requirement for essential workers (limits on transfers)
rubrics_metrics.description: Persons engaged or most recently engaged in essential activities may be employed only by an employer engaged in another essential activity, and even then only when released by the previous employer or a WMC representative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Text: “The order stipulated that persons ‘engaged or most recently engaged in essential activities [be] employed only by an employer [in] another essential activity.’ Even then they can only be employed when released by the previous employer or a WMC representative.” The controls aim to prevent movement out of war work without sufficient reasons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employer retention and dismissal standards under WMC referral
rubrics_metrics.description: No employer shall be obliged to retain a worker who is incompetent or who fails to conform to reasonable shop rules or standards of conduct; controls are designed to prevent arbitrary firing of workers referred by WMC agencies while allowing dismissal for incompetence or misconduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Passage: “1. ‘No employer shall be obliged to retain in his employ a worker who is incompetent x x x or who fails to conform to reasonable shop rules or standards of conduct.’ This paragraph implied... controls were necessary to make the hiring program effective ... On the other hand, it guaranteed that ‘insofar as it will not interfere with the war,’ ...” Also: officials said they would prevent arbitrary firing of WMC-referred workers but preserve shop standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: McNutt/WMC enforcement authorities and remedies
rubrics_metrics.description: Although the WMC order listed no explicit penalties, McNutt (acting under presidential war powers) could direct other agencies to force compliance—e.g., order War Production Board to stop materials to violators, ask procurement agencies to invoke contract penalties, cancel ration allowances, even ask the President to take over plants of violators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported enforcement capability: “The order did not mention any penalties for violation of the control regulations. WMC officials said, however, that the President had empowered Mr. McNutt to direct other government agencies to exercise any of their authority to force compliance with his orders. Thus... he could order the War Production board to shut off the flow of materials to establishments violating Mr. McNutt’s regulations; order the Army, Navy and other government procurement agencies to invoke contract penalties or even cancel ration allowances... he could ask the President to take [over] the plants of violators.” Also officials hoped persuasive methods would suffice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal to shift personal income tax to a current (as‑you‑go) basis
rubrics_metrics.description: A proposed change in assessment method: shift personal income tax assessment one year forward so taxes assessed on 1942 income would instead be assessed against 1943 income (i.e., begin 1943 paying on 1943 income), eliminating the 1942 year of assessment to reduce taxpayer debt and preserve purchasing power.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quoted argument from Mr. Ruml: “Let us turn ye tax clocks ahead one year. ... The taxes we have paid last year out of our 1942 income are taxes assessed on our incomes received in 1941. We can best solve the [debt] now ... by beginning 1943 by paying on 1943, thereby stopping out ‘the year 1942 as a year of assessment from the tax forever.’ ” Purpose: reduce intolerable hardship of income tax debt and maintain purchasing power and tax system integrity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stated broad purposes of income-tax reform
rubrics_metrics.description: Two broad purposes cited for income tax reform: (1) preservation of purchasing power and integrity of the income tax system by obtaining highest possible collections and lowest defaults; (2) humane aim of removing the constant threat of unpaid tax debt from millions of citizens.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Passage: “The purposes... are the preservation of purchasing power, and the preservation of the integrity of our income tax system through obtaining the highest possible level of collections and the lowest possible level of defaults. A second purpose springs from the personal and humane desirability of removing from millions of citizens the constant threat of unpaid tax debt...” (quoted and paraphrased in story).

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign wartime mobilization and regulatory measures (Germany/Japan/Vichy policies)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reported foreign measures include closure of luxury shops, compulsory registration of 'free professions' for service (artists, architects, lawyers, etc.), mobilization of specified age groups for service, and severe penalties for black market activities (closures, fines, imprisonment, forced labor, and in some mentions even threat of death penalty).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples in dispatches: “Shops selling luxury articles will be closed without exception. Several thousand employees of banks and insurance companies also were affected... ‘artists, painters, writers and musicians too, as members of the so-called free professions, must report’ for registration under the government's new compulsory service decree... measures against black market operations have been severe... now decreed penalties ranging from forced labor in some cases—up to death for those convicted of black market sales.” These are presented as reported national measures in Axis-occupied and Vichy territories.
